    StartersRally night pigs in blanketsCocktail franks in puff pastry, honey mustard dipHow to make it2 sheets of puff pastry24 cocktail frankfurts1 jar Dijon mustard1 egg1 tbsp sesame seeds1 jar wholegrain mustard2 tbsp honey3 tbsp mayonnaiseCut the thawed puff pastry into strips.Brush each strip with a little Dijon mustard and wrap around the cocktail frankfurts.Lay seam-side down on a lined tray, brush with the beaten egg and sprinkle with the sesame seeds.Bake at 200°C for 18 minutes until puffed and golden.Stir the wholegrain mustard into the honey and the mayonnaise for dipping and serve warm.Rock the Vote backstage crostiniCheddar, apple and walnut toasts. Mike takes the stage as AlHow to make it1 baguette3 tbsp olive oil50g walnuts2 red apples1 lemon200g vintage cheddar2 tbsp honeySlice the baguette into thin rounds, brush with the olive oil and bake at 190°C for 8 minutes until crisp.Toast the walnuts in a dry pan for 3 minutes and chop.Thinly slice the red apples and toss with the juice of half a lemon so they stay white.Top each toast with a slice of the vintage cheddar and a slice of apple.Scatter with walnuts, drizzle with the honey and finish with cracked pepper.MainsHideout cabin salmon with dill butterFoil-baked salmon over checkers. Never move your back rowHow to make it4 salmon fillets60g butter1 bunch dill2 lemons1 garlic clove800g baby potatoes3 tbsp olive oil300g green beansMash the soft butter with the chopped dill, the zest of the lemon and the crushed garlic clove.Boil the baby potatoes for 15 minutes, drain, crush lightly and toss with the olive oil and salt.Lay the salmon fillets on squares of foil, top each with a slice of the butter and a lemon slice, then seal.Bake at 200°C for 12 minutes.Fry the green beans in a hot pan with a splash of oil for 4 minutes until charred.Drake Sabitch's backwoods chilliDrake, the jumpy vet who lives in an old school bus with a grillHow to make it800g beef chuck, diced2 tbsp vegetable oil1 brown onion3 garlic cloves2 tsp ground cumin1 tbsp chipotle in adobo800g tinned crushed tomatoes400g tinned kidney beans, drained150g cornmeal100g plain flour2 tsp baking powder250ml buttermilk1 egg50g butter, melted150g sour creamBrown the beef in the oil in batches, then fry the chopped onion and garlic with the cumin for 5 minutes.Add the chipotle, tomatoes and 250ml water, cover and simmer for 1 and a half hours until the beef falls apart. Stir in the beans for the last 15 minutes.Mix the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt with the buttermilk, egg and melted butter and bake in a hot greased tin at 200°C for 20 minutes.Serve the chilli with wedges of cornbread and sour cream.DessertsNot-a-pudding apple crumbleCinnamon apple oat crumble. Not a pudding, MikeHow to make it6 Granny Smith apples60g caster sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon1 lemon100g butter100g plain flour60g rolled oats80g brown sugar600ml vanilla custardPeel and slice the Granny Smith apples and toss with the caster sugar, the cinnamon and the juice of half a lemon.Tip into the baking dish.Rub the cold butter into the plain flour, then stir in the rolled oats and the brown sugar until clumpy.Scatter over the apples.Bake at 180°C for 40 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.Warm the ready-made custard and pour over each bowl.DrinksSeattle cold brew with maple creamCold brew for the night drive into Seattle to see AlHow to make it100g ground coffee150ml thickened cream2 tbsp maple syrup1 bag ice1 L waterThe night before, stir the coarsely ground coffee into the cold water in a jug, cover and leave in the fridge for 12 hours.Strain through a fine sieve lined with paper towel.Whisk the thickened cream with the maple syrup until just thickened but still pourable.Fill the glasses with ice, pour in the cold brew and slowly pour the maple cream over the back of a spoon so it floats.
